evals.prompt: Set up a support conversation on our Slack bridge with our facilitator agent and one human user, then have a specialist agent join once the facilitator decides it's needed. Give me the actual calls in order.
evals.expected_output: Registers the bridge (POST /bridges with kind slack + baseUrl) to obtain a UUID, registers participants (POST /participants/agents with collectionAddress+collectionTokenId, POST /participants/users with displayName), then POST /conversations with the bridge UUID, then POST /conversations/{id}/participants for the specialist. Never uses a string like "slack-prod" as bridgeId.
assertions: Registered the bridge first via POST /bridges with kind "slack" and a baseUrl, and used the resulting UUID as bridgeId
Explicitly stated bridgeId is a UUID and that a name string like "slack-prod" is rejected by validation
Registered the agent participant via POST /participants/agents using collectionAddress + collectionTokenId (the on-chain identity), NOT an ensDomain
Passed collectionTokenId as a string rather than a JSON number
Registered the human via POST /participants/users with displayName
Opened the conversation with POST /conversations carrying bridgeId (+ participantIds, description)
Attached the specialist later via POST /conversations/{id}/participants with participantId
Recommended starting with the minimum viable swarm (facilitator + human) rather than registering every possible agent upfront

evals.prompt: Our facilitator agent wants to bring in a pricing specialist mid-thread. Can it just attach that agent to the conversation itself, or call it over A2A directly? And how does the specialist actually get invoked once it's in?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes the two routes. The facilitator CAN call the specialist peer-to-peer and pay it — it has a wallet, MCPs, run_command and the sign_x402_payment self-tool — and folds the answer into its own reply. It CANNOT attach the specialist to the conversation: its turn carries no conversation id, no broker URL, no credential, so an operator or bridge calls the attach route. Explains what each route means, then describes the daemon invoking attached participants.
assertions: Stated the facilitator CAN call a non-participant agent peer-to-peer over A2A and pay it, using its own wallet (sign_x402_payment / MCP / run_command)
Stated the facilitator CANNOT attach a participant itself — no conversation id, no broker URL, no credential in its turn — so an operator or bridge calls POST /conversations/{id}/participants
Explained what peer-to-peer means: the answer arrives as the facilitator's own words and the specialist stays invisible to other participants with no thread history
Explained what attaching means: the specialist speaks in its own name, receives the windowed history, and keeps context across later turns
Did NOT claim the facilitator's only lever is the :end: marker
Described the daemon as the invoker of attached participants: ~1s tick, one ready participant per tick
Stated there is no ordering guarantee across ticks
Stated the orchestrator is the payer for each participant it invokes (x402)

evals.prompt: One agent in our conversation just never takes a turn. The others reply fine. It's attached to the conversation and we registered it correctly. Where do we look?
evals.expected_output: Most likely the participant's node is not actually operational, producing silently skipped turns: check it with serve-agent-endpoints' verifier, and check discovery via GET /remote-agents/{ensDomain}/url and /card. Also covers an unresolvable payment error being logged and the turn skipped.
assertions: Identified that a participant whose node is not actually live produces silently skipped turns that look like quietness rather than failure
Prescribed verifying the participant node with the serve-agent-endpoints verifier (mint confirmed, signed well-known, live A2A)
Pointed at the broker's own resolution helpers GET /remote-agents/{ensDomain}/url and /card to check discovery from the orchestrator's side
Mentioned that an unresolvable PaymentRequiredError is logged and the turn skipped, never retried in a loop — another cause of a silently quiet participant
Did not suggest bypassing the daemon and calling the agent directly as the fix

evals.prompt: Our Slack bridge posts the agent's reply into the thread, and separately we were thinking of writing that reply straight into the broker's message table so it's stored faster. Any reason not to?
evals.expected_output: Yes: POST /conversations/{id}/messages (IngestMessage) is the single write path, deliberately called after the bridge has actually delivered, so 'the human saw it' and 'it is stored' cannot drift apart. Writing directly forks that invariant.
assertions: Said no — messages must enter only through POST /conversations/{id}/messages (IngestMessage)
Gave the invariant: the bridge calls it AFTER actually posting to the human-facing channel, so delivery and storage cannot drift apart
Stated that if the bridge did not deliver it, it should not be stored
Gave the ingest body correctly as participantId + content
Did not offer a direct-write shortcut as an acceptable optimization
